title: New Mexico v. Meta privacy-penalty ruling — Judge Francis Mathew's expected decision on New Mexico's $35–$40B ask (Cambridge Analytica case), eight days before the Q3 print
source: NEWS: a 2026-09-25 jury verdict in First Judicial District Court (Santa Fe, NM) found Meta/Facebook liable on 26 of 29 examined statements, over 43 million violations of New Mexico's Unfair Practices Act, in the state's 2021 suit over the Cambridge Analytica data-sharing scandal (Fortune, Santa Fe New Mexican, 2026-09-26). At an October 1 penalty hearing, New Mexico asked Judge Francis Mathew to impose $35–$40B; Meta's counsel argued for a $345M–$3.45B cap and signaled an appeal regardless of outcome (Reuters via Investing.com, Benzinga, KRQE, Source NM, all 2026-10-01). KRQE and Source NM both report the judge stating in court he expects to rule by late October, one account giving 2026-10-20 specifically; that date is press-reported from an oral in-court statement, not a filed scheduling order this lane has fetched itself, so NEWS: rather than ECF: is the honest prefix even though the underlying docket is federal-court-adjacent in structure (state court here, and no ECF: slot exists for a state district court regardless). Checked 2026-10-03.
notes: Discovered during meta-2026-10-28-print's 2026-10-03 pulse (adjacency sweep, item 4: geopolitical/policy -> company-specific legal). Proposed per .github/prompts/event-research.md's no-self-confirm rule; the owning lane (this id, once canonical) should re-verify the ruling date directly rather than inherit this proposal's press sourcing. WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE PRINT, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE SAME CLASS AS THE ALREADY-TRACKED YOUTH-SAFETY CHARGE: that settlement (meta-2026-10-28-print's own ledger, 09-01/09-04 rows) is a already-quantified ~$10B Q3 accrual with a known per-share drag: this is a RANGE ($345M to $40B, four orders of magnitude wide) that is STILL BEING DECIDED, lands 8 days before the print (inside the 60-day horizon, inside the 30-day all-impact window, but outside the +/-5-day print corridor, so it does not enter meta-2026-10-28-print's adjacentIds at this pulse), and a ruling anywhere near the top of the ask would be new information the Q3 call could not yet have fully priced depending on the exact ruling date relative to the quarter close. Filed `high` rather than `critical`: even the sweep's largest logged single-session reactions to adverse Meta legal news this cycle (the 08-26 youth-safety settlement, net +1.5% after giving back an initial +4.1% pop) were single-digit moves, not the print's own 10-25% class, and Meta's own proposed cap plus signaled appeal argue the modal near-term cash/P&L impact is far below the headline ask -- but a $35-40B number is roughly 2% of META's ~$1.85T market cap at the high end, large enough to rate above `medium`. SIZE IS NOT RECONCILED ACROSS SOURCES: Fortune's headline cites a theoretical $200B+ ceiling from the raw per-violation statutory maximum, which no party has asked the court to impose; the operative range argued in court is $345M (Meta's floor) to $40B (NM's ceiling), and that is the range this proposal files on. No forward test registered here -- that is the owning lane's job once it writes the canonical file.
